# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 as an initiating lesion in nucleocytoplasmic transport failure in TDP-43-linked ALS motor neurons.

Hypothesis and causal chain. In TDP-43-linked ALS (sporadic disease with TDP-43 proteinopathy and TDP-43-model motor neurons; not assumed for C9orf72 ALS), chronic ALS-relevant stress activates stress kinases that phosphorylate Nup98, an intrinsically disordered FG-repeat nucleoporin of the nuclear pore. Phosphorylation of FG-domain serine/threonine motifs is proposed to weaken the cohesive FG-network forming the pore permeability barrier, slowing Ran-dependent nuclear import. Prolonged import slowing depletes nuclear TDP-43, enabling cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing, which then amplifies transport collapse by recruiting and mislocalizing transport factors. Temporally, phosphorylation is hypothesized to be the initiating lesion; TDP-43 aggregate-associated pore disruption and stress-granule sequestration of transport factors are positioned downstream or in parallel as amplifiers.

Supported premises from the packet.
- TDP-43 pathology associates with insoluble nuclear-pore and transport components and disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems and ALS tissue [S1].
- Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of stress granules, recruit or mislocalize transport proteins, and are associated with impaired import, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death [S3].
- Stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport; altering stress-granule assembly modifies transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4].
- In C9orf72 ALS, repeat RNA perturbs RanGAP localization and import, showing transport failure can be an upstream event in at least one ALS subtype [S2]; this motivates testing upstream pore-intrinsic lesions in the TDP-43 context without generalizing across subtypes.

Speculative bridges (explicit assumptions; not established by the packet).
- Kinase and site: p38 MAPK or JNK acting on Nup98 FG-domain S/TP sites is an assumption. Unverified prior knowledge outside the packet: Nup98 and related FG-nucleoporins are disordered and are phosphorylated during mitotic pore disassembly; whether stress kinases phosphorylate them in post-mitotic neurons is untested.
- Biophysical link: that phosphorylation reduces FG-network cohesion enough to slow physiologic import rates is an assumption.
- Temporal primacy: that phosphorylation precedes nuclear TDP-43 depletion and cytoplasmic aggregation is the central untested claim.

Alternative explanations to discriminate.
1. Sequestration-first model [S4]: stress-granule sequestration of transport factors initiates failure; phosphorylation is a nonspecific stress readout.
2. Aggregate-first model [S1, S3]: cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies mechanically mislocalize or sequester pore components; phosphorylation is secondary.
3. Context model [S2]: C9orf72 repeat-RNA mechanisms drive transport defects independently of nucleoporin phosphorylation.

Discriminating preclinical test strategy.
(a) Order of events: in isogenic iPSC-derived motor neurons (TDP-43-linked ALS line versus CRISPR-corrected control) exposed to graded oxidative stress, quantify Nup98 phosphorylation (phosphoproteomics on enriched pore fractions), Ran-gradient and import-reporter kinetics by live imaging, nuclear TDP-43, and stress-granule formation at matched early time points. Prediction: phosphorylation rises before import slows, before stress-granule sequestration, and before nuclear TDP-43 loss.
(b) Perturbation: CRISPR knock-in phospho-null (S/T-to-A) and phospho-mimetic (S/T-to-D/E) Nup98 alleles at candidate sites. Prediction: phospho-null preserves import and nuclear TDP-43 under stress; phospho-mimetic impairs import without stress and without stress granules.
(c) Alternative discrimination: repeat with stress-granule assembly manipulated as in [S4]. If phospho-null rescues transport despite stress-granule formation, or stress-granule blockade rescues transport while phosphorylation persists, pore-intrinsic initiation is supported; if stress-granule blockade fully rescues and phospho-null is inert, the sequestration model is favored.
(d) Specificity: test phospho-null in C9orf72-repeat models; no effect would support subtype-specific mechanisms [S2].

Falsifying observation. Nup98 phosphorylation appearing only after stress-granule formation and import collapse, or phospho-null alleles failing to protect import and TDP-43 localization while the phospho-mimetic shows normal import, would falsify the initiating-phosphorylation hypothesis and indicate a secondary, sequestration- or aggregation-driven lesion.

Limitations. The candidate kinase and sites are assumptions; functional redundancy among FG-nucleoporins may mask single-site effects and require multi-nucleoporin mutagenesis. Phospho-mimetic substitution imperfectly mimics phosphorylation. iPSC motor neurons are immature relative to adult motor neurons, and acute stress compresses a decades-long disease course, so phosphorylation could be necessary without being sufficient. The packet sources predate 2025 and include no nucleoporin phosphoproteomics in ALS, so this remains a hypothesis, not a validated mechanism [S1-S4].

Ranked proposal:
Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 as an initiating lesion in nucleocytoplasmic transport failure in TDP-43-linked ALS motor neurons

Title: Stress-activated Nup98 phosphorylation within nuclear pores initiates nuclear import failure independently of stress-granule sequestration in TDP-43-positive ALS neurons

Mechanism and supported premises: S1 establishes that TDP-43 pathology is associated with nuclear-pore-complex disruption and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD models and patient tissue. S3 demonstrates that cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies formed independently of conventional stress granules are sufficient to impair nuclear import and deplete nuclear TDP-43, leading to cell death. S4 provides an alternative mechanism in which stress granules sequester transport factors, producing transport defects under cellular stress. The convergent premise from S1 and S3 is that nuclear transport failure is a reproducible feature of TDP-43-associated ALS pathology. None of S1–S4 identify nucleoporin phosphorylation as the molecular event within the pore.

- ASSUMPTION (unverified prior knowledge): Nup98 is a phosphorylation-regulated FG-nucleoporin whose transport or barrier function varies with phosphorylation state. This is recalled from general nuclear-pore biology outside the evidence packet.
- ASSUMPTION: A specific stress-activated kinase (e.g., p38 MAPK, proposed purely speculatively) is activated in ALS-model neurons by cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulation and phosphorylates Nup98. The identity of the kinase is entirely speculative.

1. If Nup98 phosphorylation at candidate sites precedes any measurable import defect, an initiating role is supported. If phosphorylation appears only after import failure is established, it is downstream and does not support the hypothesis.
2. Site-mutant rescue: Introduce a non-phosphorylatable Nup98 mutant (Ser→Ala at predicted sites) into ALS-model neurons. If import defects are partially rescued while stress-granule formation proceeds normally, Nup98 phosphorylation is a necessary, partially independent contributor. If rescue requires simultaneously blocking stress-granule assembly, the S4 sequestration model is better supported.
3. Sequestration control: Concomitantly measure whether importin-β and Ran remain freely distributed (not concentrated in granules) yet import remains impaired. Import impairment with unsequestered transport factors indicates a pore-intrinsic defect consistent with the hypothesis.

In sporadic ALS motor neurons carrying TDP-43 proteinopathy, sustained stress activates a kinase that phosphorylates clustered Ser/Thr residues in or near the GLFG repeats of an FG-nucleoporin — lead candidate Nup98, benchmarked against Nup153, Nup50, and Nup62. 'Selective' is tested, not asserted: TNPO1-dependent PY-NLS cargos (hnRNPA1 reporter; fluorescent TDP-43 PY-NLS and full-length TDP-43) should decline preferentially versus generic importin-α/β NLS cargo, with passive dextran flux quantified separately. 1) Reagent validation: MS-map endogenous Nup98 phospho-occupancy; the primary phospho readout is quantitative MS occupancy of knock-in tagged Nup98, with any phosphopeptide reagent accepted only after validation, avoiding reliance on an unvalidated phospho-antibody.

Asp/Glu phosphomimetic alleles are chemically weak mimics and carry corroborative weight only.
4) Orthogonal gain-of-function: chemically inducible recruitment of active candidate kinase to tagged Nup98 in unstressed neurons, bypassing phosphomimetic chemistry; acute endpoints are permeability and facilitated import at matched kinase activity.

Limitations. Scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS; C9orf72 excluded (S2). Kinase identity, residues, and direction are assumptions; packet evidence is associative; redundancy may require the full allele panel; weak phosphomimetic chemistry limits one arm; iPSC and mouse models, late post-mortem tissue, and transient phospho-signals constrain temporal resolution.

Ranked proposal:
Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Title: Stress-regulated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98, a screen-gated lead candidate among karyopherin-docking FG-nucleoporins, initiates selective Transportin-1–dependent nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

Hypothesis. In sporadic ALS motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy, sustained stress activates a kinase (p38/JNK as candidates) that phosphorylates Nup98 GLFG/FG-region serine/threonine residues; these phosphorylations are hypothesized to weaken the passive permeability barrier and impair karyopherin docking at the same pore, producing an early, selective decline in Transportin-1 (TNPO1)-dependent import — including nuclear retention of TDP-43 — before cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies [S3], stress-granule sequestration of transport factors [S4], Ran-gradient dissipation, and cell death are downstream amplifiers, not the initiating cause. C9orf72-repeat disease [S2] is out of scope, though convergence is permitted.

Supported premises. S1: NPC/transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43 and pore/transport pathology occurs in ALS tissue — co-occurrence only, no direction. S3: stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and mislocalize transport proteins — the downstream arm. S4: stress-granule assembly sequesters transport factors and impairs transport — both the sequestration alternative and the reason a phospho-null is predicted to attenuate, not abolish, the early import decline.

Declared assumptions (no packet support). A1: a stress-activated kinase phosphorylates Nup98 in adult motor neurons. A2: candidate residues are a clustered set of GLFG-region Ser/Thr sites; the mitotic Nup98 phospho-mapping analogy used to nominate them is unverified prior knowledge and is superseded by de novo MS mapping before constructs are designed. A3: directionality — phosphorylation precedes TDP-43 egress — inverts S1's co-occurrence. A4: specificity to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS. A5 (a biophysical bridge previously left implicit in the causal chain, now explicit): FG/GLFG phosphorylation simultaneously weakens the passive-diffusion barrier and reduces karyopherin-mediated facilitated import by altering karyopherin docking. All downstream work is gated on the reconstitution assay validating A5.

Alternative explanations. (1) Sequestration-first: SGs or TDP-43 assemblies deplete soluble import machinery [S4], phosphorylation irrelevant. (2) Physical displacement: insoluble TDP-43 directly distorts pores [S1], phosphorylation a bystander. (3) Genetic route: C9orf72 repeat RNA/DPR mechanisms [S2]. (4) Reverse causality: phosphorylation secondary to stress or pore disassembly.

Discriminating strategy. (1) Screen-gated nomination: comparative quantitative phospho-proteomics of affinity-purified FG-nucleoporins (Nup98, Nup62, Nup153, Nup50) from stressed human motor neurons across a stress time course. Nup98 is confirmed only if stress-regulated GLFG-region occupancy ranks among the top FG-nucleoporin hits; a dominant alternative target falsifies the Nup98-specific instantiation, recorded as such rather than silently pivoted. (2) Reagent quality: the full MS map names the residue cluster explicitly; recombinant Nup98 FG-region constructs are phosphorylated in vitro with the candidate kinase and QC'd by site-occupancy stoichiometry MS; the phospho-null carries Ala substitutions only at mapped sites. (3) Direct attribution plus the A5 node: digitonin-permeabilized neurons reconstituted with phosphorylated versus phospho-null constructs yield separately attributed outcomes — inert-dextran passive flux (barrier) and facilitated import kinetics with a two-cargo panel: an importin-α/β NLS substrate and a TNPO1/PY-NLS substrate (that TDP-43 imports via TNPO1 is unverified prior knowledge, not packet evidence). Selectivity is operational: the early decline of the TNPO1 cargo must exceed that of the importin-α/β cargo. Quantitative pull-down of TNPO1 and importin-α/β binding to phosphorylated versus phospho-null GLFG constructs mechanistically connects phosphorylation to facilitated import rather than leaving it implied. (4) Temporal tests with detection bounds: phospho-occupancy LOD is established with heavy-peptide standards; a stress-onset time course monitors phospho-occupancy, cargo import, and TDP-43 localization. Pulse–washout persistence is supportive only: self-sustaining downstream lesions (TDP-43 aggregation, SG sequestration) could maintain import failure after phosphate loss, so persistence cannot falsify initiation. (5) Perturbational test: CRISPR phospho-null panel, interpreted only after MS-verified suppression of cluster occupancy and a compensatory search bounded by the full map — no other mapped Nup98 site exceeds a pre-set occupancy-increase threshold (10 percentage points) under stress.

Decisive falsifiers (each single observation suffices). F1: with verified cluster-occupancy suppression and the bounded compensatory map, phospho-null neurons show an early-phase normalized TNPO1-cargo import decline (normalized to SG burden and soluble importin availability) indistinguishable from wild type under matched mild stress — justified because suppressed occupancy plus excluded off-cluster compensation leaves phosphorylation no causal role. F2: with LOD-validated detection, measurable import failure precedes the first detectable rise in Nup98 phospho-occupancy — justified because detection limits are excluded, so later phosphorylation cannot be the cause. Phosphomimetic data alone never count.

Staged corroboration. Only after in vitro discrimination: neuron-targeted Nup98 editing or kinase inhibition in a conditional TDP-43-mislocalization mouse (import markers, TDP-43 localization, motor behavior, survival); post-mortem ALS tissue stained with the validated phospho-Nup98 reagent, comparing neurons lacking cytoplasmic inclusions with affected neurons — corroboration only.

Limitations. Scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS; packet evidence for pore involvement is associative; kinase identity, residues, direction, and the A5 biophysics remain assumptions pending data; iPSC/mouse models may not reproduce decades-long onset; post-mortem tissue is late-stage; phosphorylation outside the Nup98 map is not bounded; phospho-signals are transient.

Ranked proposal:
Stress-regulated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98, a screen-gated lead candidate among karyopherin-docking FG-nucleoporins, initiates selective Transportin-1–dependent nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
NUP98 hyperphosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TDP-43-associated ALS motor neurons

Hypothesis. In a defined, non-C9orf72, disease-linked TDP-43 motor-neuron model, increased phosphorylation of pore-associated NUP98 weakens its retention at nuclear pores, initiating nuclear-import failure. Reduced import subsequently promotes nuclear TDP-43 depletion and persistent cytoplasmic assemblies, which amplify transport dysfunction and neuronal injury. The proposed initiating event is therefore phosphorylation-dependent pore alteration, not transport-factor sequestration. “Initiating” refers to the onset of transport failure, not the original cause of ALS. NUP98’s identity as a nucleoporin is unverified prior knowledge outside this packet; its selection and every phosphorylation-dependent step proposed here are assumptions.

Supported premises and speculative bridges. Disease-linked TDP-43 can disrupt nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport, and relevant pore pathology occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can accompany transport-factor mislocalization, impaired import, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death without conventional stress granules [S3]. These findings support investigating a pore–transport–TDP-43 feedback pathway, but neither identifies NUP98 phosphorylation as its trigger. The speculative bridges are that phosphorylation alters NUP98 pore retention, that this alteration precedes sequestration, and that preserving NUP98 retention protects neurons. No particular kinase or residue is established by the packet. Phosphorylated TDP-43 in assemblies is not evidence for phosphorylated NUP98 [S3].

Preclinical strategy. Use human iPSC-derived motor neurons carrying one preselected disease-linked TDP-43 allele and an isogenic corrected control, with independent differentiations and blinded analysis. Examine spontaneous phenotype emergence rather than relying exclusively on an imposed stress. At densely sampled time points, quantify NUP98 phosphosite occupancy by targeted phosphoproteomics, normalized to total NUP98 abundance, and distinguish pore-associated from soluble material. In matched cultures, measure endogenous NUP98 pore retention, nuclear-import reporter kinetics, passive nuclear permeability, endogenous TDP-43 localization, conventional stress granules, and persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. Include transport-factor localization, energy status, viability, and later neuronal survival to distinguish selective transport failure from generalized cellular collapse.

Causal perturbations. Identify reproducibly increased NUP98 phosphosites and fix the candidate site set before intervention experiments; do not substitute another nucleoporin if this initial gate fails. Introduce phospho-resistant substitutions at endogenous expression levels, verifying normal baseline NUP98 localization and transport. An orthogonal rescue would acutely recruit a NUP98-directed phosphatase, with targeting-only and catalytically inactive controls and measurements of neighboring pore-protein phosphorylation. The predicted result is preservation of pore retention and import before any reduction in cytoplasmic assemblies, followed by improved nuclear TDP-43 retention and survival. For sufficiency, after identifying a kinase that modifies the mapped residues, test controlled NUP98-targeted kinase recruitment in corrected neurons, with kinase-dead and phospho-resistant controls. This arm requires verified target selectivity; acidic phosphomimetics alone would not establish that authentic phosphorylation is sufficient.

Conventional stress granules could instead sequester transport factors [S4], or stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies could initiate import failure [S3], with NUP98 phosphorylation arising secondarily. Compare NUP98-directed rescue with an independently validated blockade of conventional granule assembly, while separately tracking persistent TDP-43 assemblies. Blocking conventional granules alone cannot exclude the latter route. Early rescue of import by selective NUP98 dephosphorylation, without an initial change in sequestration burden or global stress, would favor intrinsic pore alteration. Conversely, import failure preceding phosphorylation and improving only when sequestration is reduced would favor the alternative. C9orf72-repeat-associated transport defects provide a distinct context and should not be assumed to share this mechanism [S2].

Falsifying observation and limitations. The initiating hypothesis would be falsified in this model if verified, selective prevention of the disease-associated NUP98 phosphorylation increase leaves the timing and magnitude of import failure unchanged despite normal baseline pore function. Rescue of survival without rescue of import would not validate the proposed causal chain. Limitations include unknown phosphosites and kinase, imperfect targeting specificity, structural effects of phospho-resistant substitutions, and the possibility that phosphorylation compensates for rather than causes pore injury. Findings would require replication in non-C9orf72 patient-derived motor neurons and would not establish a universal ALS mechanism or a validated treatment.

Ranked proposal:
NUP98 hyperphosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TDP-43-associated ALS motor neurons

Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4]. Phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 is the proposed proximal pore modification that causes selective nuclear-import failure. A second is recruitment of those factors into stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies [S3], followed by nucleoporin mislocalization of the kind reported in [S1]. This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.

In neuronal models of TDP-43 proteinopathy relevant to sporadic ALS with TDP-43 pathology, FG-nucleoporin phosphorylation is a proposed pore-intrinsic intermediate required to sustain nuclear-import failure. Nup98 is the working candidate only if it ranks first by NPC-fraction phosphoproteomics ordered against cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies; the single-gene claim stays provisional until that ranking. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing is the initiating event. Phosphorylation of the ranked nucleoporin is proposed to maintain import suppression. Nuclear TDP-43 depletion, broader transport failure, and neuronal death are downstream responses.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components; disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and related pore pathology occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import, and transport manipulations modify phenotypes in that genetic context [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43, itself a TDP-43 modification, accumulates in the assemblies [S3]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. [S3] and [S4] separate stress-granule sequestration from a stress-granule-independent TDP-43 route. Supplied sources leave nucleoporin phosphorylation unestablished as an ALS-initiating event.

Speculative bridges. Nucleoporin identity, sites, and kinase are assumptions until the gate assigns them. Unverified prior knowledge: FG-nucleoporins are phosphorylated in mitosis or stress outside ALS. The assumed bridge is that cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies direct a kinase to the ranked nucleoporin and sustain import blockade through altered NPC composition.

Discovery gate and favored step. A site qualifies only if it maps to an NPC-localized FG-nucleoporin, exceeds a preregistered NPC-fraction occupancy threshold, and rises after assemblies form and before death markers. Rank uses qualifying-site count and occupancy, and only rank-1 Nup98 is tested; any other leader replaces Nup98 and retires the Nup98-specific claim. No qualifying site during import failure falsifies the hypothesis. Acute kinase inhibition or degradation must clear those sites while assembly burden stays matched to the phosphorylated state. The single favored step is a phosphorylation-dependent change in NPC composition, assayed by stoichiometric NPC-fraction proteomics and nucleoporin localization with the allele swap. The step is retired if phospho-null protein restores NLS-reporter import and the nuclear TDP-43 ratio while composition and localization stay indistinguishable from the assembly-positive phosphorylated state.

Alternatives are stress-granule sequestration of transport factors [S4], direct nucleoporin mislocalization by TDP-43 aggregates [S1], RanGAP mislocalization in C9orf72 models [S2], and secondary import failure from nonspecific stress.

Discriminating test. iPSC-derived motor neurons or primary rodent neurons are used with total TDP-43 held constant. Induction is locked to the [S3] de-mixing phenotype: persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies while conventional stress-granule markers stay negative. Arm 1 is that phenotype. Arm 2 uses the same TDP-43 perturbation with stress granules present. Arm 3 is stress-granule suppression alone, without TDP-43 de-mixing; NLS-reporter import must remain inside a preregistered equivalence margin of unstressed controls, or that method is retired before combination with Arm 1. Arm 4 is a C9orf72 repeat-RNA model without engineered TDP-43 assemblies [S2]. Time-resolved NPC mass spectrometry orders qualifying sites against assemblies, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death. The endogenous ranked nucleoporin is replaced at near-endogenous dosage by phospho-null or phospho-mimetic alleles limited to gate-qualified sites. Readouts are NLS-reporter import, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, NPC composition, nucleoporin and RanGAP localization, stress-granule markers, and delayed neuronal death. The Arm 1 prediction is post-assembly, pre-death phosphorylation, phospho-null rescue of import and nuclear TDP-43 despite assemblies, and persistence of the defect when stress granules are suppressed. Context specificity fails if the phospho-null versus wild-type NLS-import-rate difference in Arm 4 is at least half the Arm 1 difference on the same assay and time point.

Falsifying observations. The hypothesis is falsified when import failure lacks any site with NPC localization, prespecified stoichiometry, and pre-death precedence, or when a verified phospho-null allele leaves Arm 1 import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death unchanged in kinetics and severity. Phosphorylation confined to times after death markers is a late correlate. Co-loss of the transport defect and phosphorylation upon stress-granule suppression favors sequestration [S4]. Arm 3 import outside the equivalence margin invalidates that method. Null import effects of both allele classes, kinase inhibition that preserves assemblies and phosphosites, or an Arm 4 effect at least half the Arm 1 effect each falsify the corresponding claim.

Limitations. Sites and kinase are measurements. Ranking before allele replacement limits false negatives from redundant nucleoporin phosphorylation. Phospho-mimetics omit kinase timing and localization. Cultured neurons compress years-long human disease, and TDP-43-model results stay specific to that context. The design tests preclinical necessity and order.

Ranked proposal:
Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.

Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.

Hypothesis and context. In neuronal models of TDP-43 proteinopathy, a setting relevant to sporadic ALS with TDP-43 pathology, phosphorylation of an FG-nucleoporin is proposed as a pore-intrinsic intermediate required to sustain nuclear-import failure. Nup98 is only the pre-registered lead. The single-gene claim stays provisional until NPC-fraction phosphoproteomics ranks it first. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing is the initiating event. Nucleoporin phosphorylation is proposed to maintain import suppression. Nuclear TDP-43 depletion, broader transport failure, and neuronal death are downstream responses. The claim is limited to this TDP-43 context.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components; disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue [S1]. These data support a TDP-43–pore connection and leave the initiating modification unidentified. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import, and transport-related manipulations modify phenotypes in that genetic context [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in the assemblies [S3]. That TDP-43 modification is separate from nucleoporin phosphorylation. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. Together, [S3] and [S4] separate stress-granule sequestration from a stress-granule-independent TDP-43 route. No supplied source shows that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS.

Speculative bridges. Nup98 identity, phosphosites, and the kinase remain assumptions until the gate below is passed. Unverified prior knowledge outside this packet is that FG-nucleoporins can be phosphorylated during mitosis or stress in non-ALS cells; that background leaves the same events in ALS unestablished. The assumed bridge is that cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies direct a kinase to the ranked FG-nucleoporin and that the modification sustains import blockade. No packet source demonstrates that interaction.

Discovery gate and favored step. NPC-fraction phosphoproteomics is ordered against cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. A site cluster is included only if three pre-registered rules all hold: the phosphopeptide maps to an NPC-resident FG-nucleoporin in the NPC fraction; occupancy exceeds a pre-set fold-change and stoichiometry threshold versus matched baseline; and the rise precedes nuclear TDP-43 loss and death markers. Rank equals occupancy change weighted by temporal precedence. Nup98 enters allele tests only at rank 1; otherwise the top-ranked FG-nucleoporin replaces it. The kinase assigned by those data is then tested by inhibition or a kinase-dead allele that lowers included-site phosphorylation while imaged assemblies remain intact. The single favored step is altered FG-repeat selective permeability, read as the initial NLS-cargo import rate in permeabilized neurons supplied with excess Ran and transport factors. Quantitative NPC-composition mass spectrometry is the retirement assay: restored import rate with disease-matched subunit stoichiometry retires a composition mechanism; normalized stoichiometry without import rescue retires the FG-permeability step.

Alternatives. Transport factors may be sequestered in stress granules, so import fails without a covalent pore change [S4]. TDP-43 aggregates may mislocalize nucleoporins directly, leaving phosphorylation as a bystander [S1]. In C9orf72 models, RanGAP mislocalization may explain import failure without FG-nucleoporin phosphorylation [S2]. Import failure may also follow nonspecific cellular stress.

Discriminating preclinical test. Four arms use iPSC-derived motor neurons. Arm 1 locks induction to a cytoplasm-enriched TDP-43 de-mixing construct that forms persistent assemblies while G3BP1 stays dispersed, matching the stress-granule-independent route [S3]; constructs that nucleate conventional stress granules are excluded. Arm 2 uses the same TDP-43 perturbation with stress granules intact. Arm 3 applies one pre-registered intervention that prevents G3BP1-positive granules, without TDP-43 de-mixing, and must keep NLS-reporter import inside a pre-registered null window of unstressed baseline; a method that itself impairs import is invalid. Arm 4 is a C9orf72 repeat-RNA model without engineered TDP-43 assemblies [S2]. Included sites only are swapped at near-endogenous dosage for phospho-null or phospho-mimetic alleles, with total TDP-43 held constant. Readouts are NLS-reporter import, permeabilized initial import rate, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, NPC composition, nucleoporin and RanGAP localization, stress-granule markers, and delayed death. Predictions in arm 1: included phosphorylation follows assemblies and precedes death; phospho-null and on-target kinase blockade each preserve permeabilized import rate and nuclear TDP-43 despite intact assemblies. Context-specificity fails if the phospho-null gain in NLS import rate in arm 4 exceeds 0.25 times the gain in arm 1.

Falsifying observation. Absence of any site meeting the three inclusion rules while import is already impaired falsifies the hypothesis before allele construction. Confirmed absence of the mapped modification on phospho-null protein, with unchanged kinetics and severity of import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death in arm 1, also falsifies it. Phosphorylation only after death markers marks a late correlate. Joint disappearance of the transport defect and of phosphorylation when stress granules are suppressed favors sequestration [S4]. No import phenotype for both phospho-null and phospho-mimetic alleles falsifies a functional role for the included sites. Kinase blockade that leaves import impaired while assemblies remain intact falsifies phosphorylation as the required intermediate. An arm-4 effect above the 0.25 bound retires the context-specific claim.

Limitations. Site and kinase identity must be measured. Redundant phosphorylation of other nucleoporins can yield a false-negative single-gene result. Phospho-mimetic substitutions omit kinase timing and localization. Cultured neurons compress a years-long human disease, and TDP-43-model results stay tied to the tested context rather than transferring automatically to C9orf72 or SOD1 ALS. The design tests necessity and order in preclinical systems and stops short of therapy validation.

Ranked proposal:
Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy

Insoluble TDP-43 associates with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell models, with related pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. The same study leaves nucleoporin phosphorylation unidentified. C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and reduced nuclear import, and transport or repeat-RNA manipulations modify model phenotypes, within a genotype-specific route [S2]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can arise without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and associate with cell death [S3]. MECHANISM AND CAUSAL CHAIN. Scope: TDP-43 proteinopathy-dominant ALS contexts; not claimed universal across subtypes. S1: TDP-43 aggregates associate with insoluble pore and transport components, disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport, and pore pathology is seen in ALS tissue; this establishes NPC-TDP-43 coupling in tissue without directionality. S3: persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 demixing can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalizes transport-associated proteins, impairs transport, depletes nuclear TDP-43, and links to cell death, with phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulating in these assemblies. S4: stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and altering granule assembly modifies defects and phenotypes. No supplied passage shows nucleoporin phosphorylation; establishing that polarity is the aim here.

SPECULATIVE BRIDGES (assumptions, not packet-supported). (a) Unverified prior knowledge: mitotic NPC disassembly involves CDK-family phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporins including Nup98; the packet contains no nucleoporin phosphorylation data. (b) Assumption: mitotic-site phosphorylation can be reactivated in postmitotic diseased neurons, for example through cell-cycle-related kinase reactivation. (c) Model assumption: partial phosphorylation yields measurable permeability increase and Ran-gradient perturbation below full disassembly. (d) Bridge: gradient collapse reduces TDP-43 import efficiency enough to initiate cytoplasmic exposure before any sequestration.

(a) Granule-first: TDP-43 demixing [S3] or stress granules [S4] sequester transport factors, with pore phosphorylation a secondary consequence; read together, S3 and S4 caution that conventional granules need not mediate every defect. (b) C9orf72 repeat-RNA-first mechanisms [S2] act directly on RanGAP or transport without pore phosphorylation, so this hypothesis must be tested per genetic context. (c) Transport failure secondary to generalized stress or metabolic collapse. (d) Dominant phosphorylation of other nucleoporins (inner-ring or basket nucleoporins) instead of Nup98.

# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
NUP98 phosphorylation as an initiating pore-retention lesion in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons

Hypothesis. In TARDBP M337V motor neurons, early nuclear TDP-43 dysfunction alters kinase/phosphatase signaling, increasing phosphorylation at an empirically identified NUP98 site. This modification weakens scaffold binding and pore retention, initiating nuclear-import failure before detectable cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. Import failure subsequently amplifies nuclear TDP-43 depletion and neuronal dysfunction. “Initiating” concerns transport failure, not the genetic mutation or every ALS subtype. M337V disease association and NUP98 domain architecture are unverified prior knowledge here.

Supported premises. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport; pore pathology also occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can impair import without conventional stress granules [S3], whereas stress granules provide another transport-factor-sequestration route [S4]. None establishes phosphorylation-first ordering. C9orf72-associated transport disruption is a boundary contrast, not supporting evidence for this TARDBP–NUP98 mechanism [S2]. The entire proposed upstream nuclear-dysfunction–phosphorylation–scaffold-binding chain remains speculative.

Site identity and structural rationale. Ser606 is presently unanchored and will remain a provisional candidate, not a fixed premise. Begin with unbiased comparative NUP98 phosphoproteomics in mutant and isogenic-corrected motor neurons, followed by targeted, site-localized mass-spectrometry validation in independent cultures. Map reproducible changes onto the expressed isoform’s FG-rich and pore-association regions, using verified sequence and structural annotations rather than assuming Ser606’s location. Before engineering, lock one reproducibly elevated, temporally early site with a plausible scaffold-contact relationship; Ser606 advances only if qualified. The proposed biophysical effect is phosphate-dependent weakening of a mapped scaffold interaction, not an unsupported assertion about FG cohesion. If no site qualifies, stop this mechanism in these cultures rather than indefinitely switching sites.

Upstream mechanism and specificity. The proposed ordering lacks an early nuclear readout. Measure nuclear TDP-43 activity with a splicing reporter experimentally validated by depletion and wild-type rescue, alongside transcript profiling of candidate kinase/phosphatase regulators. A link between altered splicing and phosphorylation remains an assumption until directly tested; splicing dysfunction could occur with unchanged NUP98 phosphorylation. JNK is a provisional kinase candidate based on unverified prior knowledge of stress-kinase biology. Require motif compatibility, direct phosphorylation of the selected site, and concordant effects of selective inhibition and genetic suppression before assigning it this role; an inhibitor rescue alone is insufficient.

An isogenic contrast alone cannot exclude generic mutant-cell stress. Add inducible, endogenous-range nuclear-retained wild-type TDP-43 rescue with expression-matched controls, verifying restored splicing. Ask whether phosphorylation normalizes before changes in assembly burden or measured metabolic/proteostatic stress. Stress-matched corrected neurons provide another comparator. Rescue-associated normalization would support TDP-43 dependence but cannot exclude unmeasured stress or broad rescue effects.

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Use multiple independently derived motor-neuron lines, isogenic controls, blinded measurements, and longitudinal sampling. Quantify site occupancy relative to total NUP98, pore localization, nuclear-import kinetics, nuclear/cytoplasmic TDP-43, transport-factor sequestration, conventional granules, firing, and survival. Measure passive permeability, ATP, and general stress to distinguish selective import failure from cellular deterioration. The predicted ordering is nuclear functional change, phosphorylation, diminished pore retention, import failure, then TDP-43 redistribution and dysfunction; temporal precedence alone is insufficient.

Test necessity with an endogenous phospho-resistant substitution at the locked site and orthogonal inducible NUP98-directed phosphatase recruitment. Include sequence-reverted, catalytically inactive, and untargeted controls; assess neighboring sites, NUP98 abundance, and baseline transport. Both interventions should preserve retention and import before reducing assembly burden, followed by functional benefit. Compare authentic site-specifically phosphorylated and unphosphorylated NUP98 in scaffold-binding and pore-reconstitution assays. Feasibility is uncertain; phosphomimetics alone would not establish sufficiency, and biochemical sufficiency would not establish neuronal sufficiency.

Alternatives and falsification. Factorial experiments should compare phosphorylation-directed protection with independently validated suppression of conventional granules and cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, because granule suppression alone does not address [S3]. Confirm intervention effects on phosphorylation, sequestration, and stress. Sequestration-first or generalized-stress explanations predict that phosphorylation follows transport failure or becomes dispensable when those processes are controlled. A decisive falsification would be verified prevention of the selected phosphorylation event by both orthogonal interventions, with baseline pore function preserved, yet unchanged import-failure timing and neuronal dysfunction. Consistently post-failure phosphorylation would also reject its initiating role.

Limitations. Undetected assemblies, mutation-induced structural changes, off-target dephosphorylation, and incomplete stress matching could confound inference. Failure of the JNK arm rejects that kinase assignment, not independently the NUP98 hypothesis. Cultures omit aging and non-neuronal influences. Positive findings would establish a bounded preclinical mechanism, not a universal ALS cause or validated treatment.

Ranked proposal:
NUP98 phosphorylation as an initiating pore-retention lesion in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons

This mark initiates the transport lesion in this TARDBP setting: FG cohesion weakens, passive permeability rises, and Ran/NTF2 flux collapses before persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, with later nuclear TDP-43 loss. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies that form independent of conventional stress granules mislocalize transport proteins, impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and accompany cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in them [S3]. Stress sequesters transport factors in stress granules and impairs transport [S4]. Nucleoporin phosphorylation, any WEE1 splice, and event order remain unspecified in [S1]-[S4].

Unverified prior knowledge assigns FG/GLFG cohesion to passive permeability, pore anchoring to the NUP98 C-terminus, mitotic disassembly to CDK1 phosphorylation of NUP98, CDK1 restraint to Wee1 on Tyr15, and some cassette-exon choices to TDP-43. Phosphorylated TDP-43 in assemblies [S3] leaves demixing causation untested.
